# Source Evaluation

> Copy of [Source Evaluation](https://github.com/SOsintOps/intelligence-field-notes/blob/main/docs/source-evaluation.md) from [Intelligence Field Notes](https://github.com/SOsintOps/intelligence-field-notes) 0.1.1. The original is the reference; this copy is here for offline use.

Information becomes intelligence only after it has been evaluated. These notes use one system everywhere: the **4 x 4 system** of the UNODC [*Criminal Intelligence: Manual for Analysts*](https://www.unodc.org/documents/organized-crime/Law-Enforcement/Criminal_Intelligence_for_Analysts.pdf), the one used by Europol and widely adopted by police agencies. It is simple, and the manual explains why that is a virtue: grading information on personal knowledge rather than on plausibility makes it less subjective.

## Three Principles
1.  Evaluation is **professional judgement**, not personal feeling.
2.  The **source** and the **information** are graded **separately**. A reliable source can pass on hearsay; an unknown source can hand over a genuine document.
3.  Grade **as close to the source as possible**, at the moment the item enters the case, not at the end.

## Source Reliability
| Grade | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| **A** | No doubt about authenticity, trustworthiness, integrity or competence; or a history of complete reliability |
| **B** | A source whose information has in most instances proved reliable |
| **C** | A source whose information has in most instances proved unreliable |
| **X** | Reliability cannot be judged |

## Information Validity
| Grade | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1** | No doubt about accuracy |
| **2** | Known personally to the source but not to the person passing it on; logical in itself; agrees with other information on the subject |
| **3** | Not known personally to the source, but corroborated by other information already recorded |
| **4** | Not known personally to the source and cannot be independently corroborated |

The two grades travel together as a code: `B2`, `X4`, `A1`. Some agencies add a **handling code** for who may receive the report, giving codes such as `B24`; for open-source work the [Traffic Light Protocol](https://www.first.org/tlp/) usually does that job (see [Report Writing](report-writing.md)).

A link or a fact is **confirmed** when its grade is A1, A2, B1 or B2; any other grade makes it **unconfirmed**. In a link chart, confirmed links are drawn solid and unconfirmed ones dashed.

## Who Is the Source in OSINT?
The platform is not the source. A post on a social network, a page in a company register and an article in a newspaper are all "open", and none is graded by the website it sits on.
- **The source** is whoever produced the information: the account holder, the journalist and their outlet, the registry that keeps the record, the person quoted. An official register maintained by law (a company registry, a court record) usually earns an `A`; an anonymous account with no history is `X` until it builds one.
- **The information** is graded on the relationship between the source and what it says: a company director filing their own accounts is reporting first-hand (`2` or `1` if verified); a forum user repeating what "everyone knows" is hearsay (`4` unless corroborated, `3` if corroborated).
- **Corroboration must be independent.** Ten channels forwarding the same post are one source, not ten. Trace each item to its origin before you count it.
- **Self-reported data is the subject's claim**, not a fact about the subject: a profile's stated location, employer or age is graded as what the subject says about themselves.
- **Tool output is not a source.** A search engine, an aggregator, a breach-lookup service or an AI model returns pointers. Grade the underlying record they point to, after you have retrieved it.

## Provenance and Preservation
A grade is only as good as your ability to show where the item came from. For every item record:
- the URL or origin, and the date and time of capture in UTC;
- the method and tool used to capture it;
- a SHA-256 hash of the captured file;
- the grade, with a one-line reason when it is not obvious.

## Sanitisation
After grading, a report for dissemination should not reveal more about its sources than the reader needs. Remove details that would identify a confidential human source, split material that only a few people could know, and keep the source register (the list that maps `S1`, `S2`... to real origins) separate from the report when the report travels further than the case team.

## Converting from the 6 x 6 (Admiralty) System
Many agencies and older templates use the 6 x 6 system (source A to F, information 1 to 6, also called the Admiralty or NATO code). The UNODC manual notes that the two systems differ by more than the number of grades, especially for information: the 6 x 6 scale grades how *plausible* information is, the 4 x 4 scale grades how *close* the source was to it. So:
- **Source:** 6 x 6 `A` and `B` correspond to 4 x 4 `A` and `B`; `C`, `D` and `E` (fairly reliable to unreliable) fall in 4 x 4 `C`; `F` (cannot be judged) is 4 x 4 `X`.
- **Information:** do not translate the number; **re-grade** the item by asking the 4 x 4 questions (did the source know it personally? is it corroborated?).

## Further Reading
- **"Criminal Intelligence: Manual for Analysts"** (UNODC, 2011) - Chapter 4, "Evaluation of source and data": the 4 x 4 and 6 x 6 tables and sanitisation. [PDF](https://www.unodc.org/documents/organized-crime/Law-Enforcement/Criminal_Intelligence_for_Analysts.pdf)
- **"Criminal Intelligence: Manual for Front-line Law Enforcement"** (UNODC, 2010) - The same system from the side of the officer who collects and reports. [PDF](https://www.unodc.org/documents/organized-crime/Law-Enforcement/Criminal_Intelligence_for_Front_Line_Law_Enforcement.pdf)
- **"ICD 206: Sourcing Requirements for Disseminated Analytic Products"** (ODNI) - Source descriptors and source summary statements. [PDF](https://www.dni.gov/files/documents/ICD/ICD-206.pdf)
- **"Verification Handbook"** (European Journalism Centre) - Practical verification of accounts, images and video. [verificationhandbook.com](https://verificationhandbook.com/)
